chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! A man from our companions pelted the Jamarah on the Day of Sacrifice and shaved before he slaughtered.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was visited on the Day of Sacrifice by groups of Muslims who said,

O Messenger of Allah! We slaughtered before we pelted, and we shaved before we slaughtered, and there did not remain anything from what was befitting for them that they should bring forward except that they delayed it, and there was nothing from what was befitting for them that they should delay except that they brought it forward.
So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'No blame, no blame.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim performs Hajj rituals in a different order than prescribed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the principle of *la haraj* (no hardship) in Hajj rituals, illustrating the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) leniency when early Muslims confused the sequence of stoning, shaving, and slaughtering. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a foundational evidence for the non-obligatory nature of strict ritual order (*taratib*) in Hajj, distinguishing between essential pillars and recommended sequences. It underscores the practical flexibility granted to pilgrims to accommodate human error without invalidating the pilgrimage.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws the 2nd, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! A man from our companions pelted the Rocks (Jamarah) on the day of the sacrifice and shaved off (his head) before he slaughtered’. So heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahazwj, when it was the day of the sacrifice, a group of Muslims came over to himsaww, and they said, ‘O Rasool-Allahsaww! We slaughtered before we pelted (the Jamaraat), and we shaved off (our heads) before we slaughtered’, and there did not remain anything from what was befitting for them that they should bring it forwards, except that they delayed it, and there was nothing from what was befitting for them that they should be delaying it, except that they brought it forward.
So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Nothing wrong! Nothing wrong!’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja’far, al-Thani, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, a man of our people has thrown pebbles on al-Jamar on the day of al-Nahr (slaughtering the offering, 10th of Dhu al-Hajjah) and shaved before slaughtering his offering.’ He (the Imam) said, ’It was the day of al-Nahr (slaughtering the offering, 10th of Dhu al-Hajjah) when many groups of Muslim people came to the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause. They said, “O Messenger of Allah, we slaughtered before throwing pebbles and shaved before slaughtering our offering. Nothing was left of the acts that were before but they had delayed or that which was later they had done it before.”

The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, said, “You are not required to face any complexity. There is no difficulty (to cause suffering).””’
